title: An isolated prime of a finite type algebra over a field has finite residue field
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $B$ be a finite type (finitely generated) $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. If $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}B$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] has singleton $\{\mathfrak p\}$ open in $\operatorname{Spec}B$, then $\mathfrak p$ is a maximal ideal of $B$, and the residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak p)=B_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pB_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], with its field extension structure from $k\to B\to\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-pc-field-extension], is finite over $k$, i.e. $\dim_k\kappa(\mathfrak p)<\infty$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00PJ (algebra-lemma-isolated-point, line 30106), implication (1) => (6), using Lemmas 00G1 and 00G3 to make an isolated prime maximal and Theorem 00FV (algebra-theorem-nullstellensatz, line 6524) for finiteness of the residue field of a maximal ideal

proof.text:
*$\mathfrak p$ is maximal.* The closed subsets of $\operatorname{Spec}B$ in the Zariski topology [def-weil-affine-spectrum] are the sets $V(I)=\{\mathfrak q:\ I\subseteq\mathfrak q\}$ for ideals $I\subseteq B$. Since $\{\mathfrak p\}$ is open, its complement is $V(I)$ for some ideal $I$, so $\{\mathfrak p\}=\{\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}B:\ I
ot\subseteq\mathfrak q\}$. In particular $I
ot\subseteq\mathfrak p$; choose $f\in I$ with $f
otin\mathfrak p$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-field-prime-intersection-maximal] (the Jacobson property of $B$) there is a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\supseteq\mathfrak p$ with $f
otin\mathfrak m$. Then $I
ot\subseteq\mathfrak m$, so $\mathfrak m
otin V(I)$, i.e. $\mathfrak m\in\{\mathfrak p\}$, hence $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak m$ is maximal. (This is the argument of Lemma 00G3, that the closed points of $V(J)$ are dense in it, applied to $Z=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and the open set $\{\mathfrak p\}$.)

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00PJ (algebra-lemma-isolated-point, line 30106), proof of (1) => (2), first sentences: Spec(S) is Jacobson by Lemmas 00G1 and 00G3, so the isolated point q is closed; Lemma 00G3 (algebra-lemma-jacobson, line 6692), first half of its proof; Lemma 00G1 (line 6668)

proof.text: *$\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is a finite type $k$-algebra.* Write $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak p$, now maximal, so $B/\mathfrak m$ is a field. The composite $B\to B_{\mathfrak m}\to\kappa(\mathfrak m)=B_{\mathfrak m}/\mathfrak mB_{\mathfrak m}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is surjective: for $b\in B$ and $s\in B\setminus\mathfrak m$ choose $t\in B$ with $st-1\in\mathfrak m$ (the class of $s$ is invertible in the field $B/\mathfrak m$); then $b/s-bt/1=b(1-st)/s\in\mathfrak mB_{\mathfrak m}$, so $b/s$ and the image of $bt$ have the same class in $\kappa(\mathfrak m)$. If $b_1,\dots,b_n$ generate $B$ as a $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], their images generate $\kappa(\mathfrak m)$ as a $k$-algebra (a $k$-algebra surjection carries polynomials in the $b_i$ to the same polynomials in their images). So $\kappa(\mathfrak m)$ is a field which is a finite type $k$-algebra via $k\to B\to\kappa(\mathfrak m)$.

source.place: Algebra, Theorem 00FV (algebra-theorem-nullstellensatz, line 6524), last sentence 'The same is true in any finite type k-algebra' and the first paragraph of its proof (reduction to a quotient of the polynomial ring, where kappa(m) = B/m)

proof.text: *$\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is finite over $k$.* By step 2, $K=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ with $k\to B\to K$ is a field that is a finitely generated $k$-algebra; [lem-weil-pbc-zariski-lemma] gives $\dim_kK<\infty$, i.e. $K/k$ is a finite field extension [def-pc-field-extension], with exactly the $k$-structure of the statement.

Statement kept, with 'finitely generated k-algebra' now citing def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra and the intermediate conclusion 'p is maximal' made explicit. Proof in three steps: (1) isolated => maximal by the argument of 00G3 using the new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-field-prime-intersection-maximal (00G1, isJacobsonRing_of_finiteType + isJacobsonRing_iff_prime_eq); (2) for maximal m, B -> kappa(m) is surjective, so kappa(m) is a field of finite type over k (elementary, written out); (3) the existing Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-zariski-lemma (00FV(1)/0CY7) gives finiteness.
